previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman was admitted for worsening bilateral lower extremity edema and cellulitis, with a history of chronic lymphedema, morbid obesity, and recurrent infections. She presented with increased swelling, erythema, and mild shortness of breath, and was found to have leukocytosis and stable renal function. Treatment included a 10-day course of IV clindamycin for cellulitis, IV diuresis with furosemide that was later transitioned to oral bumetanide, and management of a supratherapeutic INR due to antibiotic interaction by temporarily holding warfarin and initiating a heparin drip. Her infection resolved, INR stabilized, and she was discharged home on her baseline medications, including warfarin and bumetanide, with instructions to complete a course of fluconazole for oral thrush and follow up for lab monitoring. Despite aggressive diuresis, weight reduction was minimal due to the challenges of fluid management in severe lymphedema.

 Outpatient Providers: Ms. ___ is a ___ year old female with

initiated on IV vancomycin (pre-medicated with Benadryl given 
history of red man's syndrome) 1000mg Q12H which was continued

Dermatology was consulted on hospital day #2 and agreed with a 
trial of antibiotics despite no obvious exam features consistent 
with cellulitis. By hospital day #4, her exam was unchanged and 
her white blood cell count remained elevated, which actually is 
chronic for this patient. The patient agreed with a trial off 
antibiotics, so vancomycin was discontinued. Her exam, WBC 
count, and fever curve were trended off antibiotics. Her 
extremities continued to be intermittently erythematous and 
warm, attributed to venous stasis changes. 

# Chronic lymphedema: Pt has long history of this. Has failed 
wraps, pumps, and ___ clinic as outpatient. She is
